title: Standby comms draft: capacity incident window & employee Q&A
content:
Purpose and context:
- Quick working draft for internal comms if we need a short-notice employee-facing announcement about the capacity maintenance/incident window or degraded-latency events. Intended audience: all employees (primary), eng teams, CS/oncall.
- This is a writable scratchpad: multiple versions (short, long, leader talking points, Q+A). Keep it lean and easily copy/paste into Slack/email/All-Hands slides.

TL;DR (short Slack-ready):
- Heads-up: We have a scheduled capacity remediation window tonight 10:30pm–11:30pm PT for rolling driver updates and KV-cache rebalancing. You may see transient increased latency (20–50% of requests) and brief request failures for <5 minutes during rollouts. No customer data at risk. Ops will post live updates to #sys-ops. (Sign: SRE team)

Alternate higher-alert TL;DR (if incident escalates):
- Active incident: Some hosted API requests are seeing elevated latency and error rates. We’re in rollback/mitigation. If you have high-priority customer workflows, switch to dedicated/private fallbacks or pause automated jobs. Follow #incident-ops for updates.

Background (one-paragraph summary):
- Tonight’s work addresses an edge-case in the scheduler that can cause uneven GPU assignment under bursty load, leading to degraded tail latency on certain model variants. Mitigation plan: staggered driver patch + KV rebalance + targeted canaries, with automated fallback to smaller-model variants if latency exceeds thresholds. We expect the majority of requests to be unaffected; risk window is ~60 minutes during the roll.

Owners & escalation contacts:
- Primary comms owner: Eden Park (eng-sre) — draft+post updates.
- Oncall lead: Jonas Lee — live incident commander until resolved.
- SRE escalation: Maya Chen (infra lead) — cross-region capacity.
- Customer success lead (customer-facing notices): Sahana Iyer — coordinate messaging for impacted customers.
- Exec contact: Rowan Patel (CRO) — for any escalations requiring leadership intervention.

Channels for external/internal updates:
- Internal: #incident-ops (live updates), #all-hands-broadcast (for summary update after resolution), email to eng-all for postmortem summary.
- External/customer: CS will use customer-incident templates; only escalate to customer-facing posts if impact > X tokens/min or SLA thresholds hit (TBD with CS).

Suggested Slack post (short, internal):
- [SRE] Quick notice: We’re doing a rolling capacity remediation now (10:30–11:30pm PT). You may see transient latency and a small number of request failures. We will post progress here and ping if any action is needed. No customer data exposure.

Suggested Slack post (if incident escalates):
- [INCIDENT] Elevated latency and errors detected for hosted API in us-west-2. Mitigation in progress (rollback + canary). If you manage customer jobs, consider pausing batch runs or shifting to Dedicated endpoints. Ongoing updates in #incident-ops.

Email template for eng-all (longer, for end of day):
- Subject: Nightly capacity remediation — possible transient latency tonight
- Body: Hi all, small note that SRE will run a capacity remediation tonight starting at 10:30pm PT (target window up to 1 hour). Work includes driver patching and KV-cache rebalancing. Expected user impact: short-lived latency spikes and sporadic request failures; we’ll monitor and rollback if needed. Please avoid running heavy experiments during this window. We’ll follow up in the morning with outcomes and next steps.

Leader talking points (for on-call/EMs to read on quick sync):
- What: rolling capacity fix to prevent uneven GPU assignment under bursty load.
- Why: prevents tail-latency incidents we saw in Jan; targeted, low-risk change.
- Impact: minor transient latency in a subset of requests; no data risk.
- Ask: minimize heavy batch runs during the hour; CS and SRE will coordinate customer checks.

Q&A (common questions + suggested answers) — editable:
Q: Will customer requests lose data?
A: No — this work is infrastructure-level; we don’t touch customer payloads or storage. Retries are safe and idempotent for most flows.

Q: How long will the work take?
A: Target 60 minutes including canary. If rollback triggers we will focus on quick revert which could add ~15–30 minutes.

Q: Should I stop my experiment/job?
A: If it’s non-urgent, yes — pause until the window completes. If you run critical customer jobs, talk to CS and SRE for options (dedicated/private fallback, manual scheduling).

Q: Where will updates be posted?
A: #incident-ops for live play-by-play; summary to #all-hands-broadcast and eng-all after resolution.

Q: Do we need to inform customers now?
A: Not proactively unless impact crosses SLA thresholds. CS is on standby to notify impacted customers.

Comms checklist (for Eden / comms owner) — quick TODOs:
- [ ] Post initial short Slack notice 15 minutes before start.
- [ ] Confirm canary health checks are green before broad rollout.
- [ ] Provide 15/30/45 minute updates in #incident-ops.
- [ ] If rollback occurs, post clear timestamped note and ETA.
- [ ] Draft postmortem bulleted summary for eng-all within 24 hours.

Postmortem & follow-ups (draft language for later):
- Will include incident timeline, root cause, RCA action items, customer impact, and preventive work (scheduling heuristics, monitoring improvements). Owner for RCA: Maya Chen. Target: shipping mitigations in the next sprint.

Open questions / TODOs (notes for collaborators):
- Decide SLA threshold for customer notification (ask CS: % err rate over X minutes).
- Confirm whether dedicated endpoints should auto-failover for high-profile customers during these windows.
- Decide whether to mark this as a scheduled maintenance in the status page (ops product) or treat as regular incident.

Notes & rough script for short all-hands mention (if asked live):
- We ran a planned cap fix to address scheduler imbalance causing tail latency; it was completed with minimal impact. SRE ran canaries, rolled changes, and validated metrics. Postmortem will follow. Thanks to the oncall team.

Raw scratch ideas (keep editable):
- Consider a short A/B experiment: auto-announce maintenance windows for low-traffic hours to reduce surprise.
- Add a one-click pause for all scheduled experiments in console during ops windows.
- Quick telemetry snippet to include in the morning summary: p50/p95/p99 delta, #requests failed, affected model variants.

Appendix: quick links & references:
- Incident ticket: INF-4231 (linked above)
- Runtime PR for rollback behavior: PR#678 (linked above)
- Monitoring dashboard: (placeholder) - add grafana link before posting

— End of draft.

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight; prefer Slack short posts + one consolidated email. After run, copy the postmortem bullet list into Confluence and link back here.
